title: Keep Gemini permission choices manual during unrelated pending runtime resets
outcome: A generic pending runtime reset does not reject a Gemini request under a misleading Yolo-mode-change reason; uncertain grant authority stays with the existing manual decision owner.
acceptance: An unrelated reset on an active Yolo process does not fabricate a mode-change-specific refusal or reject a genuine multi-choice request solely because the generic reset flag is set.

Router-level behavior tests cover an unrelated reset and a multi-choice permission request, preserving opaque request/option IDs and the existing manual-card ownership without an automatic persistent grant.
Stop, stale runtime, read-only custody and pending native-mode authority checks retain their independent behavior.
